Apple is reportedly having its annual sales in India surpass US$10 billion for the first time last fiscal year.

To achieve this in a country where the per capita annual income is less than US$3,000 is remarkable—especially when iPhones are priced higher in India than in the U.S....

For years, iPhone sales in India were negligible for Apple. But in recent years, thanks to the growth of the local economy and Apple's ability to finally open Apple Stores locally, the situation has changed dramatically.

Bloomberg reported the latest milestone today.

Given the low per capita income, and the fact that iPhones are manufactured in India, you might expect them to be much cheaper there than in the U.S. In reality, however, high taxes mean Apple products are actually priced higher in India than in the U.S.

Apple tries to offset the difference to some extent by partnering with banks to offer credit card rebates.

Around a quarter of iPhones are currently made in India, but most are sold to the U.S. market. Apple restructured its logistics arrangements specifically to avoid U.S. tariffs on Chinese imports.
